podcast.title: Artwork Designer
podcast.body: Peter Saville, chief art design guy at Factory Records, did design work for No Means No (referred to as "Noam D" in the transcript). "He did everything from gig posters to album design for Joy Division New Order, Roxas music, Swade, pulp, Martha Nemuffins, and Noam D."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Geographical Origins and Evolution
podcast.body: No Means No originated in Victoria, Canada, and later relocated to Vancouver. Their sound occupied a unique space blending hardcore and metal, and they are recognized for containing elements that would later define post-hardcore. "And then there was no means no, who started in Victoria and later moved to Vancouver. They ended up occupying a space somewhere between hardcore and metal."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Iconic Vancouver Hardcore Band
podcast.body: No Means No is recognized as a prominent band from Vancouver's 70s and 80s hardcore scene, which was a defining musical characteristic of the city during that era. Matthew Good referenced them while discussing the loss of Vancouver's influential musical "edge." "I can't see no means no or DOA or adversity or anyone doing that."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Matt Good: In His Own Words - Part 2

podcast.title: Kurt Cobain's Endorsement
podcast.body: The album "WRONG" was highly praised, notably by Kurt Cobain prior to Nirvana's mainstream success. "Excellent record. And won the cut the year of a pre-never-mine Kurt Cobain. He loved this record."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Post-Hardcore Influence
podcast.body: Their distinctive sound, blending hardcore and metal, showcased elements that foreshadowed what would become known as post-hardcore, influencing bands such as At The Drive-In, The Rollins Band, Alexisonfire, Billy Talent, The Deftones, and Silverstein. "If you listen carefully to what they did, you can hear elements of what would become known as post-hardcore, a sound that would later birth groups like at the drive-in, Rawlins Band, Alexis on Fire, Billy Talent, The Death Tones and Silverstein."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Victoria Band History
xref.body: NoMeansNo is identified as a "fine Canadian punk band" from Victoria, British Columbia, who have been active since the late 1970s. The band is known for insisting on doing things their own way, which sometimes leads them into trouble. "no means no, a fine Canadian punk band from Victoria who have been around since the late 1970s."
